slides.texte_overlay:
Little things that make you
surprisingly good at
talking to women
Talk to her the same way you talk to your friends. Relaxed, honest, a bit funny. Changing into a different person around women always feels forced.
Ask about her opinions, not just her job. "What's a film everyone loves that you can't stand?" Opinions lead to fun debates and real connection.
Notice what she's into and ask more. A book in her bag, a festival wristband, paint on her hands. Real curiosity beats any rehearsed line.
Be comfortable with a pause. Silence doesn't need filling every second. A relaxed pause and a smile show you're enjoying the moment, not performing.
Bring something interesting to the table. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a good story makes any conversation flow naturally.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A good story makes any conversation flow naturally.

slides.texte_overlay: Share a bit of yourself too. A funny fail, a small dream, a passion. Conversation is a two-way street, and openness makes her want to open up.
Respect the signs she's done talking. Short answers, looking away, friends waiting. Wish her a good evening with a smile. Respect is always attractive.
